stated: The Conservative Party will invest £300 million to ensure all parents can access wraparound childcare before and after school by September 2026.

source.quote: And to give working parents more flexibility, we are investing £300 million so that all parents can access wraparound childcare before and after school by September 2026.

bearing_set.reason: Before/after-school wraparound care directly removes a primary barrier to parental employment (especially maternal), affecting hours worked, real earnings, and in-work poverty.

£300m public investment to subsidise wraparound provision addresses a significant household cost burden; if it reduces or caps parental childcare fees, real disposable income rises for working families.

Before-and-after-school care provision directly affects children's educational access and supports the attainment gap — structured wraparound provision is associated with improved outcomes for children from disadvantaged households who currently lack access.

membership_note: The policy's primary effects are on parental work participation (O4), children's educational opportunity and attainment gap (O7), and household childcare costs as a cost-of-living pressure (O2). A fiscal cost (O12) exists but £300m is insufficiently large to materially shift the debt path on its own and the policy does not specify unfunded status, so O12 does not clear the non-negligible bar. Inequality effects (O14) are real but are largely captured through O4 (enabling low-income maternal employment) rather than needing a separate bearing.
